cf.title: amcheck: add index-all-keys-match verification for B-Tree

input.subject: amcheck: add index-all-keys-match verification for B-Tree

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the thread shows real demand from two independent users. Before commit, the proposal needs to name a corruption case that heapallindexed misses (already-exists-1). It also needs agreement that bt_index_check() with all options off may read heap size (maintenance-fit-2). The remaining points (maintenance-fit-1, standards-compat-2) are fixable, but only a committer who knows amcheck can sign off on the risk of false corruption reports.

brief.title: amcheck: verify that B-Tree index keys match their heap tuples
brief.problem: Existing amcheck checks miss index entries whose stored key differs from the key of the heap tuple they point to, because the index structure stays valid. The author hit such corruption with UTF-8 Russian locales around hyphens and spaces, and wants a tool to investigate it, possibly for corruption his own company caused.
brief.proposed_design: A new indexallkeysmatch option makes a dedicated sequential heap scan that fingerprints visible (key, TID) pairs in a Bloom filter. The index scan probes each leaf tuple and each posting list entry, and on a Bloom miss fetches the visible heap tuple through table_fetch_tid(), following HOT chains, and compares keys with FormIndexDatum. A second patch makes both functions always report leaf TIDs beyond heap EOF, and reports unused or out-of-range heap slots only under ShareLock.
user_visible_surface: New boolean parameter indexallkeysmatch on bt_index_check() and bt_index_parent_check().
amcheck extension version bump to 1.6 with an upgrade script amcheck--1.5--1.6.sql.
New corruption errors, for example "index tuple in index ... does not match heap tuple" and errors for index TIDs pointing to missing heap pages.
bt_index_check() and bt_index_parent_check() now always report index TIDs beyond heap EOF, even with all options off, unless the main fork is absent.
With both heapallindexed and indexallkeysmatch on, two Bloom filters are allocated, each up to maintenance_work_mem.
author_claims: Detects key mismatches that heapallindexed and structural checks miss, including inside posting lists before an ordering violation shows up.
The unconditional beyond-EOF check is the first way Postgres can notice a lost or short relation segment, and it costs nearly nothing.
With the MVCC fetch, key-match verification is safe under AccessShareLock, so no stronger lock is needed in bt_index_check().
Jakub Wartak measured indexallkeysmatch at about 5 times a bare bt_index_check, and about 2 times heapallindexed.
The whole pg_amcheck test suite passes with the main-fork-absent skip.
brief.thread_state: Zsolt Parragi, Wenbo Lin and Jakub Wartak reviewed, and Jakub co-authored; Wenbo's concurrent VACUUM false positive and Jakub's API, docs and standby-cache points were addressed in v7. No one has replied to v7, and the author's own TODO on bt_normalize_tuple() corner cases is only partly reported as done.
unclear: Whether an always-on heap size check in bt_index_check() is an acceptable behavior change for users who expect a heap-free index check.
Whether all known heapallindexed normalization issues the author listed (TOAST, varlena forms) are covered for the reverse direction.
How the check behaves with collation or locale changes, the reported root cause, beyond the expression-swap test.
Whether a single shared heap scan for heapallindexed and indexallkeysmatch was considered beyond the author's complexity objection.
Whether a committer has looked at the design; the listed reviewer Álvaro Herrera has no message in the thread.

prior_attempts.title: amcheck verification for GiST
prior_attempts.quote: My main concern now is the heavyweight lock strength needed by the new function.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Geoghegan questioned whether the checks are safe under an AccessShareLock, since Heikki's v6 had used a ShareLock. He doubted that the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() applies here and asked how concurrent page deletion could affect it. Andrey Borodin did not answer these questions for about two months, so Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 was a new GiST checker whose safety under AccessShareLock was not answered. This proposal uses an MVCC fetch under AccessShareLock for the key check and reports unused heap slots only under ShareLock.

objections.title: heapallindexed may already report the key mismatches this targets
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA suspects the hyphen or space collation corruption from message #1 and runs bt_index_check with heapallindexed and indexallkeysmatch on. That costs about twice the time of heapallindexed alone, and two Bloom filters. heapallindexed alone would already have reported the corrupt index entry.
objections.argument: heapallindexed fingerprints each index tuple with its heap TID, and expands posting lists into one fingerprint per TID. It then probes with the key formed from each visible heap tuple. An index entry "foobar" at TID T, with "foo-bar" in the heap at T, gives a Bloom miss and an error, so the TAP test's expression swap should fail heapallindexed too. Message #1 only says that structural checks missed the corruption. The v1 commit message says heapallindexed cannot catch it but names no case, so the gain may be limited to extra wrong-key entries next to a correct one, and to clearer error messages.
objections.author_must_show: Which concrete corruption, such as the Russian-locale case or the expression-swap test, passes heapallindexed but fails indexallkeysmatch?

critic.reasoning: heapallindexed fingerprints each index tuple with its TID and probes with the key formed from the visible heap tuple, so "foobar" against "foo-bar" at one TID gives an error. The thread names no case that passes heapallindexed and fails the new check.

objections.title: Always-on heap size check changes a heap-free function inside an option patch
objections.failure_scenario: An operator runs pg_amcheck with --exclude-table on a table known to be damaged and still checks its indexes, as the 003_check test does. With v7, bt_index_check with all options off now reads that heap's size and reports corruption whenever a higher segment is missing. The excluded table again fails the run.
objections.argument: Messages #9 and #10 show that pg_amcheck depends on bt_index_check not touching the heap, and v7 handles this with one special case: it skips the check only when segment 0 is absent. That rule covers the test case but leaves the behavior change in place for partly lost heaps. The change also lands in a patch that is otherwise about an opt-in option. The beyond-EOF check is cheap and independent, so it could be proposed and discussed as its own commit.
objections.author_must_show: Why should bt_index_check with every option off start reading heap state, and why ship this in the indexallkeysmatch series rather than as a separate patch?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 weighs the cost and keeps the check unconditional, but the skip covers only an absent main fork. An excluded table with a lost higher segment still fails the index check, and no committer has commented on that change.

objections.title: Second user of bt_normalize_tuple() widens a known source of false corruption reports
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs bt_index_check with indexallkeysmatch on a table whose varlena values reach the index in a different but equivalent form. The check raises ERRCODE_INDEX_CORRUPTED "does not match heap tuple". The user reindexes or restores from backup for corruption that does not exist, and the bug surfaces only as a field report.
objections.argument: Message #10 says normalization has been a rich source of subtle heapallindexed bugs, and message #12 cites three follow-up fixes. Message #14 reports only that the existing TOAST and short varlena cases now run with the new option. It does not say the planned review of all known cases is complete. Each future change to datum representation must now keep two comparison directions in agreement, and a missed case shows up as a false corruption error. Reviewers of the earlier uniqueness check in [P1] called a false corruption report unacceptable.
objections.author_must_show: Which normalization cases differ between the heap-to-index and index-to-heap directions, and how does each one avoid a false corruption report?

precedents.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index

critic.reasoning: Message #10 says the normalization corner cases apply to the new direction, and message #14 reports only the existing TOAST and short varlena tests. [P1] concerned a message that said an index only might be corrupt, so it gives weak support here.

objections.title: pg_amcheck gets no option for indexallkeysmatch
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA who checks a cluster with pg_amcheck wants the new key-match check across all indexes. pg_amcheck has --heapallindexed, --rootdescend and --checkunique but no flag for this, so the DBA must write their own loop over bt_index_check() calls. Per-index error handling and parallelism are lost.
objections.argument: The touched files in all three v7 patches are under contrib/amcheck and doc/src/sgml/amcheck.sgml only, and none touches src/bin/pg_amcheck. Every earlier B-Tree option is exposed through pg_amcheck, which also has to choose call signatures by installed amcheck version. Leaving the new option out makes the feature incomplete for its main audience.
objections.author_must_show: Will pg_amcheck get an option for indexallkeysmatch, and how will it handle servers with amcheck older than 1.6?

critic.reasoning: The v7 file lists contain nothing under src/bin/pg_amcheck, and the thread never discusses a pg_amcheck option. pg_amcheck exposes the earlier B-Tree options, and the review summarized in [P1] asked for the same integration.

refuted.title: bt_index_check() with all options off now reads heap size and can fail
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs a nightly pg_amcheck job, or plain bt_index_check(idx), that has always checked index structure only. After a minor-free major upgrade the job reports corruption because a heap segment is short, or it meets a new heap access path the job did not expect. The operator finds out from an alert, with no option to restore the old index-only behaviour.
refuted.argument: v7-0002 checks leaf TIDs against heap size "regardless of indexallkeysmatch", so the default call changes meaning. Message #10 says bt_index_check() historically never touches the heap and pg_amcheck relies on that. The patch keeps that contract only through a narrow skip for an absent main fork, which treats one test case and leaves other heap states open. The author argues an opt-in flag would rarely run, but an existing entry point in contrib that changes behaviour by default is usually avoided, especially when the C library changes before ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should the beyond-EOF check change the default behaviour of the existing functions instead of being a separate option or function that callers enable?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which states the same default-behaviour change with a more concrete scenario. The scenario here is partly a true corruption report, which is not a failure.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: amcheck 1.6 changes the signatures of bt_index_check() and bt_index_parent_check(), which pg_amcheck and scripts call.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The reverse check evaluates index expressions with FormIndexDatum, and its new error messages may print key values.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: v7-0002 makes both existing functions report TIDs beyond heap EOF with every option off.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: bt_normalize_tuple() gets a second comparison direction, and a missed case appears as a false corruption error.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: heapallindexed may already report the key mismatch from message #1, so the added coverage needs a named case.

questions: Which concrete corruption, such as the Russian-locale case or the expression-swap test, passes heapallindexed but fails indexallkeysmatch?
Why should bt_index_check() with every option off start reading heap size, and why is this in the indexallkeysmatch series instead of a separate patch?
What should pg_amcheck report for the indexes of an excluded table whose heap has lost a higher segment but still has segment 0?
Which normalization cases differ between the heap-to-index and index-to-heap directions, and how does each one avoid a false corruption report?
Will pg_amcheck get an option for indexallkeysmatch, and how will it handle servers with amcheck older than 1.6?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows amcheck's B-Tree verification and the heapallindexed normalization code. Álvaro Herrera is listed as reviewer on the CommitFest entry but has no message in the thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for every false "does not match heap tuple" report caused by a missed normalization case. The owner also signs for the changed default behaviour of bt_index_check() for as long as amcheck ships.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revisions through v7 in response to each review and moved the entry to the next CommitFest himself. Jakub Wartak joined as co-author.

priority.reason: The check serves people who investigate index corruption, and its cost falls only on those who enable it, apart from the always-on heap size check. The entry has been in 4 CommitFests, v7 has no reply, and no committer has posted.

provisional_note: Without the code, the normalization coverage for the reverse direction could not be checked. Two security points are also unchecked: whether FormIndexDatum runs under the restricted security context amcheck already uses, and whether error messages print key values the caller cannot otherwise read.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.

precedents_retrieved.title: partial heap only tuples
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds partial heap only tuples (PHOT), so an update creates new index tuples only for indexes whose columns changed, and those index tuples point to the new heap tuple. Index scans follow a PHOT chain only while their own indexed columns stay unchanged, and pruning of PHOT chains is restricted.

No updated patch was posted, so the entry was returned with feedback in November 2021. The visible messages show design concerns, such as index create/drop handling and long-term heap fragmentation, but no objection that decided the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add reverse collations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a REVERSE option to create collation, so a text column can sort in reverse order under a collation such as "C_backwards". The goal is to let a single row comparison like (a, b collate "C_backwards", c) > (...) express keyset pagination when the ORDER BY mixes ASC and DESC.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the planner would not know that a reverse collation pairs with a backward scan of an index on the forward collation, so queries would not be optimized as users expect. He saw it as a repeat of reverse-sort operator classes, which ASC/DESC indexes made obsolete, and noted it only covers text columns. He suggested a more general row comparison instead, such as ROW(a,b) OPERATOR(<, >) ROW(c,d). The visible messages do not show the withdrawal itself.

just a gotcha, because queries won't get optimized the way users

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove extra Sort node above a btree-compatible Index Scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the planner's pathkey comparison so that an index from a B-tree-compatible access method in a different operator family is treated as matching the ORDER BY. precedents_retrieved.title: Scan key push down to heap
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch turns simple "var op const" quals on a sequential scan into scan keys and tests them with HeapKeyTest, so that rows are filtered before full qual evaluation. A later version moved the test from heapam into nodeSeqScan.c, used slot_getattr, split scan keys from other quals at plan time, and showed them as "Scan Key" in explain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas asked for a redesign of the first version: the split between scan keys and other quals had to happen at plan time with a new SeqScanPath, and the keys had to be rechecked in SeqRecheck. Andres Freund then questioned the special case for seqscans and suggested that expression evaluation itself should handle scankey-style OpExprs, so the gain would reach all nodes. The author agreed to try this, and the entry moved to the next commitfest as waiting on author before it was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
Reverted commit(s): Restructure libpq's handling of send failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1f39a1c06 implemented write-failure postponement in pqSendSome,
which is above SSL/GSS processing.  However, we've now seen failures
indicating that (some versions of?) OpenSSL have a tendency to report
write failures prematurely too.  Hence, move the primary responsibility
for postponing write failures down to pqsecure_raw_write(), below
SSL/GSS processing.  pqSendSome now sets write_failed only in corner
cases where we'd lost the connection already.

A side-effect of this change is that errors detected in the SSL/GSS
layer itself will be reported immediately (as if they were read
errors) rather than being postponed like write errors.  That's
reverting an effect of 1f39a1c06, and I think it's fine: if there's
not a socket-level error, it's hard to be sure whether an OpenSSL
error ought to be considered a read or write failure anyway.

Another important point is that write-failure postponement is now
effective during connection setup.  OpenSSL's misbehavior of this
sort occurs during SSL_connect(), so that's a change we want.

Per bug #17391 from Nazir Bilal Yavuz.  Possibly this should be
back-patched, but I think it prudent to let it age awhile in HEAD
first.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent covers the same idea. The one related concern, amcheck lock strength in P2, is answered in the thread. P1 was returned for inactivity and for false-positive reporting, and this thread fixed its own false-positive case in v6 and v7.
The new parameter is appended to both signatures and follows the heapallindexed naming, so the SQL surface itself fits existing practice.

The proposal is a read-only contrib/amcheck check. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol change or core ABI, only an extension version bump to 1.6 with an upgrade script. The one cross-node point, a stale cached heap size on a standby, was raised in message #11 and answered in message #14. A standby query whose snapshot is broken by replayed pruning is cancelled through a recovery conflict, which gives no false report.

The proposal adds no new privilege path. amcheck functions are not granted to PUBLIC by default, the new option sits inside existing amcheck functions, and heapallindexed already evaluates index expressions, so the reverse check adds no new kind of code execution. The material does not show the code, so two points could not be checked. One is whether FormIndexDatum runs under the table-owner restricted security context that amcheck already uses. The other is whether the new error messages print key values that the caller could not otherwise read.
Hot-path cost falls only on users who enable the option. For committability, no committer has posted in the thread, and the listed reviewer Álvaro Herrera is silent.
The unconditional beyond-EOF check has no existing equivalent in amcheck or core that I can name, so it draws no objection from this angle.

The material shows real demand. Message #1 reports production B-Tree corruption in which index keys differed from heap keys under UTF-8 Russian locales and existing amcheck checks did not catch it. Message #8 adds a second, independent need from Jakub Wartak: detecting a lost heap segment, which today shows up only as silent row loss. Other users pay little, because the costly reverse check runs only when indexallkeysmatch is set. The one always-on part is the beyond-EOF comparison, and whether that behavior change is acceptable is a design question for another angle.
